motion: Does divine hiddenness count against a perfectly loving God?

bridges.description: Show why nonresistant unbelief counts against a perfectly loving God that seeks relationship.
Show why even one genuine nonresistant nonbeliever contacts the universal loving-God claim.
Ask why a loving God leaves intellectual belief as a barrier to relationship or salvation.
Show how hiddenness remains compatible with a perfectly loving God's purposes and justice.
Challenge public confidence that nonresistance can be identified despite desire-laden belief formation.
Separate present propositional belief from relationship and ultimate salvation, including possible postmortem reconciliation.

sections.title: Scope of the hiddenness challenge
sections.rationale: Both sides delimit the motion to a perfectly loving God rather than generic theism.

sections.title: The one-exception claim and its probability
sections.rationale: This section tests whether one nonresistant case is enough and whether such a case has adequate support.

sections.title: Postmortem reconciliation
sections.rationale: Jones offers eventual reconciliation as a compatibility response and Paulogia tests its theological basis.

sections.title: Private experience and public evidence
sections.rationale: The speakers dispute whether hiddenness is independent public evidence or a personal conclusion.

sections.title: Introspection and personal force
sections.rationale: Paulogia's stated openness and Jones's conclusion-versus-argument reply bear directly on personal rational force.

sections.title: Loving disclosure and unequal evidence
sections.rationale: Paulogia argues that a loving God should bridge an open person's gap; Jones limits the public reach of that report.

sections.title: Belief, relationship, and salvation
sections.rationale: The final burden concerns whether present belief is a necessary gateway and whether eventual justice answers hiddenness.

coverageAudit.retainedScopeSummary: Every event in the approved main discussion, approximately 7:58–58:46, was reviewed. The selected inventory preserves the narrowed loving-God motion; reasonable versus nonresistant unbelief; the one-exception and probability dispute; desire and reason; postmortem salvation, Romans 1, continuing freedom and sanctification; private versus public force; contents versus causes of thought; belief versus relationship; self-serving disclosure; unequal evidence; and belief versus salvation.

majorLines.description: Narrowed motion and generic-theism limitation at 7:58–9:10
majorLines.omissionRationale: The follow-on agreement about Schellenberg's elaboration adds source background but no distinct adopted burden beyond the selected scope moves.

majorLines.description: Reason, desire, nonresistance, and the one-person universal claim at 9:21–16:19
majorLines.omissionRationale: The Obama and spouse examples remain within their selected complete arguments; repeated restatements of the if-versus-probability distinction are not separate moves.

majorLines.description: Postmortem salvation, Romans 1, missionary implications, freedom, hell, and sanctification at 16:19–25:25
majorLines.omissionRationale: Jones's intervening eschatology explanation for missionary work and brief acknowledgement are supporting context; his speculative limitation and continuing-freedom mechanism are retained explicitly.

majorLines.description: Reported motivated-reasoning studies and the majority-versus-exception reply at 25:25–31:21
majorLines.omissionRationale: Jones's Islam self-example is retained inside the study move only as supporting evidence; his later limited-perspective allowance is omitted because postmortem compatibility and public-access limits are selected in fuller form elsewhere.

majorLines.description: Thought contents, cognitive causes, therapy, deconversion, and personal rational force at 31:21–36:16
majorLines.omissionRationale: The excluded snack joke supplies nothing. Jones's nonselected elaboration about subconscious causes is represented by the therapy move, while Paulogia's narrower contents claim and later self-application remain distinct selected moves.

majorLines.description: Moser's self-serving disclosure answer, the residual minority, and limited public access at 37:11–47:10
majorLines.omissionRationale: Repeated analogies to religious experience are contained within the selected public-access move; Paulogia's explicit limitation on using hiddenness to tell Jones that God does not exist is preserved in the coverage qualification below.

majorLines.description: Possible honest rejection, perfect justice, belief prerequisites, and closing self-bias method at 44:57–58:46
majorLines.omissionRationale: The uninformed-person and safer-ignorance examples apply the same belief/salvation distinction. Jones's initial self-bias and addiction analogy remain coverage context, while the focused fallibility and public-method argument is selected. Excluded audience material contributes no assessed substance.

coverageAudit.qualificationPreservation: Paulogia removes generic-God disproof, states outside the final selected row that hiddenness is not a simple public argument telling Jones God does not exist, and accepts shared desire scrutiny. Jones allows possible nonresistant unbelief, treats desire as an influence rather than the absence of reason, admits postmortem details are speculative, and distinguishes present belief from ultimate relationship and salvation.

moves.scoredClaimOwnership: This row credits Paulogia's own source claim that the argument need only conclude that no perfectly loving God exists, rather than that no God exists. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Michael Jones's own source claim that divine hiddenness challenges Christian theism but does not refute basic deism or generic theism. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Paulogia's own source claim that reasonable or nonresistant unbelief need not be free of emotion or desire; it requires that sufficient new information could overcome those influences. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Michael Jones's own source claim that reason and desire are not distinct belief categories because both operate together in ordinary belief formation. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Paulogia's own source claim that even one capable person who is nonresistantly in unbelief gives divine hiddenness evidential force. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Michael Jones's own source claim that the relevant question is whether a genuinely nonresistant person is probable, not merely conceivable. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Paulogia's own source claim that the claim that an honest nonbeliever may receive another opportunity after death needs a theological basis. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Michael Jones's own source claim that postmortem salvation is a scripturally and philosophically possible answer, though its mechanics remain speculative. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Paulogia's own source claim that the excuse for honest unbelief appears to conflict with the Romans claim that everyone is without excuse and sufficiently aware. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Michael Jones's own source claim that romans 1 concerns people who know of God and willingly reject that knowledge, not modern atheists who never received it. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Paulogia's own source claim that if honest unbelievers can be reconciled after death, the reason for sending missionaries becomes unclear. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Michael Jones's own source claim that freedom and possible acceptance of God need not end at death, while reconciliation still requires difficult sanctification rather than automatic admission. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

moderatorPrompt.summary: Shannon asks Jones to clarify whether a nonresistant nonbeliever could receive salvation after death; only Jones's own ensuing freedom and sanctification reasoning is scored.

moves.scoredClaimOwnership: This row credits Michael Jones's own source claim that divine hiddenness is either a personal experiential report or a conclusion derived from other evidence, rather than an independent public argument. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Michael Jones's own source claim that reported psychological evidence makes wholly nonresistant belief formation less probable, although it does not make it impossible. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Paulogia's own source claim that the cited psychology supports a tendency, not a universal rule, and leaves room for the single exception the argument needs. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Paulogia's own source claim that a person can know the present content of their thoughts even if they cannot know that the thoughts are accurate or fully explain their causes. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Michael Jones's own source claim that people often lack transparent access to the deeper dynamics producing their thoughts. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Paulogia's own source claim that after honest introspection, Paulogia sees no attachment he would refuse to surrender and says he would return to Christianity if the intellectual problem were resolved. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Michael Jones's own source claim that paulogia's account is a conclusion reached from other intellectual considerations, not an independent hiddenness argument. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Paulogia's own source claim that after removing as much identifiable resistance as possible, continued inability to believe makes absence of a loving God a rational personal conclusion. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.
This row credits Michael Jones's own source claim that belief and relationship should not be modeled as a rigid two-step sequence. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Michael Jones's own source claim that demanding propositional knowledge from God on preferred terms may be self-serving and may hinder the transformed relationship God seeks. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Paulogia's own source claim that an account of self-serving demands by many people leaves unanswered the minority who legitimately cannot cross the belief barrier. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Paulogia's own source claim that a loving God has provided much stronger evidence to some people, so failing to bridge an open nonbeliever's gap counts against perfect love. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Michael Jones's own source claim that a report that God has not bridged one person's gap remains private evidence others cannot independently assess. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Michael Jones's own source claim that even if honest rejection exists, a perfectly loving and just God can eventually forgive, heal, and provide missing information. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Paulogia's own source claim that if belief is a prerequisite to salvation or relationship, a loving God should provide enough disclosure that no willing person remains blocked at that stage. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Michael Jones's own source claim that recognizing possible error should lead people to compare beliefs through explanatory scope, power, plausibility, ad hoc cost, illumination, and respectful conversation. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.

This row credits Paulogia's own source claim that both sides should keep checking whether desire prevents truth from overcoming prior commitments. No premise asserted by Shannon Q is treated as the guest's evidence.
